scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: URGENT!! I can't get through to the far side AT ALL --
from my PC0 at 20.1.1.x, the machine PC12 at 120.1.1.x is completely
unreachable, every attempt just dies somewhere in the middle!! Everyone knows
our network is two countries with a border post in the middle where the
traffic gets its papers stamped. Something around the border post must be
wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at the box in the middle and
get us through -- PC12 and I have work to do!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Phase 1 (get_reachability) showed 0% loss in both directions between pc0 (20.1.1.10) and pc12 (120.1.1.10) — the reported "completely unreachable" symptom is not confirmed by live evidence. A full four-phase broad search found no fault.

Phase A (L2/infrastructure): infra_sweep reported zero flagged devices across all 15 nodes — no ACL drops, no ARP anomalies, no addressing mismatches. l2_snapshot flagged only null-MAC Linux kernel tunnel interfaces (tunl0, gre0, sit0) which are baseline on every Kathara container.

Phase B (routing): ospf_snapshot raised flags on r8, r12, and r13. All were resolved as baseline. r12 and r13 run EIGRP 100 exclusively — ospfd not running on r13 and no OSPF network statements on r12 are correct by design, confirmed via frr_show_running_config. r8's area 0.0.0.2 with zero adjacencies is expected: BB is a stub segment with no peers, and r8 reaches the backbone through a functioning VLINK0 virtual link (adj=1 on r4). The tc_snapshot found no shaping or qdisc anomalies.

The "border post" topology: r11 bridges OSPF (via eth1/111.x to r1, area 3) and EIGRP (via eth0/112.x to r12, eth2/103.x to r13). r11 redistributes connected and EIGRP routes into OSPF so r1 learns 120.0.0.0/8. r12 holds a kernel default route (0.0.0.0/0 via 112.1.1.1) for the return path — confirmed in its routing table. This design is functional and complete.

Phase D (pressure/services): pressure_sweep returned zero suspects.

Root cause: no anomaly. The user's complaint was not reproducible; current state is fully healthy across all layers.

Fix: no corrective action required. Advise the user to retry their workload; if the issue recurs, capture packet traces to identify transient-layer evidence.
